summary: Adversarial verify, 2026-11-08 00:10-00:25 Central. Load was 3.6-4.1, so frame timing is not_measured. No heavy harness was run because nothing has changed. `git diff ac10d5386^ -- art/out/fighters/rishal/` is empty, and no tracked rishal source, content or out file is modified. A GLB parse of all three skins shows 27 joints (root...toe.R, plus x_visor_ridge, prop.L/R and x_knife_tip_l/r), no cloth, tabard or scarf bone, the materials body and accent, and 17 clips. I re-read the 3 portraits, the 3 splashes and the match-pair shot myself. All 4 majors stand as majors. One factual point in M2 is corrected: the Chalkline neck is dark slate, not brown, though the striation still shows. Sensitivity: the helm is a hard segmented dome with a crescent crest, so it is not a soft, tall or pointed hood (ruling 3 and the hood ruling's hard-part clause apply). Every face plate carries ink brow, nose and mouth carving (crop scratchpad/v/f_rishal_lamplit_portrait.png), so it is not a blank mannequin. The wood neck pushes the read toward an artist's mannequin, which keeps it at major, not blocker; the previous verifier (closing2 Nov 7) made the same call. Score 7.0, NOT ON PAR (below 7.5, no blocker). The backlog is M1 to M4.

findings.title: The splashes are flatly lit model renders on the plate, with the faces unreadable
findings.what: Base: a stiff wide stance with one knife pointed and a flat cool ambient on a pale figure, and the face plate a few pixels. There is a faint contact shadow on the ledge, so the base is grounded. Chalkline: a crouch-leap, with the near foot touching the ledge edge and the rear foot in the air over the chasm, and no scene light on the figure. All three read as renders composited onto a painted plate.
findings.evidence: art/out/fighters/rishal/splash.png, rishal_chalkline_splash.png, rishal_lamplit_splash.png (Nov 4, unchanged); downscales in scratchpad/v/splash.png and rishal_chalkline_splash.png; art/blender/fighters/rishal.py:79 (SPLASH victory t 0.92).
findings.gauge: A LoL splash is a painted illustration: a narrative pose, the face or weapon as the value focal point, light shared with the scene, and the figure grounded.
findings.fix: As the reviewer proposes: a Glint Cut beat on a chalk spire ledge, a warm rim from the plate's sun side, the face plate as the top value, contact occlusion, and an overpaint pass.
findings.verifierNote: Re-read all three. The base does have a weak ledge shadow, so the reviewer's 'no contact' applies only to Chalkline, where the rear foot is airborne on purpose (a leap). The core claim, unpainted flat-lit renders with tiny dark faces, holds. Major, not blocker: the cards exist and are on-model.

findings.title: A bare striated neck under a smooth oval face plate; the brief's chalk gorget is missing
findings.what: The base and Lamplit show a brown, vertically striated wood-grain neck between the cowl and the face plate. Chalkline's is dark slate but still striated. With the smooth oval plate it pushes toward an artist's-mannequin read at portrait size.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/v/portrait.png, rishal_lamplit_portrait.png, rishal_chalkline_portrait.png; crop scratchpad/v/f_rishal_lamplit_portrait.png. _design/fighters/rishal.md:61 and :77 name a chalk gorget, and `grep -i gorget art/blender/fighters/rishal.py` finds none. rishal.py:195 sets neck #3E3A38 for Chalkline.
findings.gauge: LoL portraits frame a designed neck and collar with no unexplained primitive in the hero crop.
findings.fix: Build the brief's carved chalk gorget (2-3 lames up to the visor chin line), repaint any exposed neck as flat under-suit slate, and re-render the portraits and icon.
findings.verifierNote: Correction: 'every portrait shows a brown wood neck' is wrong for Chalkline (dark slate), though it is striated there too. Tested as a blocker under the 'blank mannequin' rule and rejected: the face plate carries carved brow, nose and mouth lines on all three skins. It is the nearest sensitivity risk and should be fixed first in the backlog.

findings.title: No secondary motion: 27 joints and no tabard, scarf or crest follow-through
findings.what: There is no cloth or scarf bone in any of the three skins, so run, dash, casts and ult have no lag or settle on the tabard.
findings.evidence: The GLB parse of rishal.glb, rishal_chalkline.glb and rishal_lamplit.glb gives 27 identical joints with no x_scarf. _design/fighters/rishal.md:62 names a one-bone x_scarf.
findings.gauge: LoL cloth and accessories lag, overshoot and settle on every move.
findings.fix: Add tabard flap bones and x_scarf, and bake a spring lag with overshoot into run, dash, cast_a3 and cast_ult, plus a settle in the attack recoveries.
findings.verifierNote: Joint list reproduced. The brief calls the scarf 'rigid, one-bone', so the brief does not itself require lag. Even so, the missing bone and the stiff tabard are a real gap against the gauge. Major holds.

findings.title: At the gameplay camera he is a pale blue-white figure with no own hue; the crimson signature never reaches the model
findings.what: In the match frame Rishal (orange ring) is pale blue-white, and the neighbouring figure (white ring) is pale grey-blue in nearly the same value. Only the silhouette and the ring separate them. Crimson #B3004A appears only on the icon and in VFX.
findings.gauge: LoL champions carry one ownable hue or value mass that reads at the gameplay camera before the silhouette.
findings.fix: Give him one owned mid-dark mass in VALE's palette (a slate-crimson tabard field or crimson knife grips and bindings, about 6-8 % of the facing) and a mid-slate nape cap, then check against the lineup hue tool.
findings.verifierNote: Visually confirmed in the cited shot. It is a single frame, but the palette data supports the claim structurally.
